chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The zakat of the ornaments is its lending it.
ai.seo_question: What is the method of paying zakat on gold and silver jewelry according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from Al-Kafi is interpreted by scholars such as Al-Majlisi to mean that the 'loan' (‘ariyah) refers to the act of giving the jewelry in use or the profit derived from it, rather than a literal lending transaction. This ruling distinguishes jewelry from trade goods or livestock, emphasizing that zakat is due on the intrinsic value or utility of the ornaments rather than their physical transfer. The interpretation highlights the Shia view that zakat on personal adornments is linked to their economic benefit or market value, differing slightly from some Sunni schools that may require payment from the principal.
